description: Ghostfin is a long-range, hybrid-electric unmanned undersea vehicle (UUV) designed and built in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The vehicle is capable of transiting more than 1,000 nautical miles, remaining at sea for up to 30 days, and carrying up to 250 pounds of configurable mission payload. Ghostfin is capable of four-person launch and recovery, shipboard launch, underwater launch from a dry-deck shelter, and air delivery, enabling flexible employment across a range of operational environments. Ghostfin extends UUV reach beyond traditional operating envelopes and enables distributed effects at operationally significant ranges. Its modular payload bay can accommodate Albacore-provided, vendor-provided, and Government-provided payloads, supporting mission sets including ISR, kinetic one-way attack, mine countermeasures, anti-submarine warfare, counter-UUV operations, and electronic and non-kinetic attack. This flexibility allows operators to hold adversary forces and maritime infrastructure at risk while reducing exposure to high-value manned platforms, providing a high-performance, scalable capability for maritime operations.
differentiator: Ghostfin’s technology centers on a compact hybrid-electric power system, comprised of a JP-8 combustion engine and batteries, specifically designed for small and medium UUVs, overcoming the fundamental limitations that have historically constrained battery-only UUV platforms. This represents a significant engineering advancement, as hybrid-electric systems have previously been limited to much larger UUV platforms due to size and complexity constraints. This capability enables a 10-20x improvement in range compared with battery-powered sUUV platforms and a 5-10x range improvement compared with battery-powered mUUVs, despite a significantly reduced size. Ghostfin also features a modular payload bay capable of carrying up to 250 pounds, allowing rapid reconfiguration across mission sets. Albacore has currently developed its own ISR, kinetic defeat, and minesweeping payloads for Ghostfin. Government-provided and other vendor-provided payloads can also easily be integrated into Ghostfin. This payload flexibility enables a single platform to support evolving operational needs without redesigning the vehicle.
q1_problem_understanding: Ghostfin enhances UUVGRU, SOF dive teams, and Marine Corps stand-in units' capabilities by closing the undersea distance gap and providing long-endurance undersea sensing and effects delivery. With 1,000 nautical miles of range and up to 30 days of endurance, Ghostfin can reach contested waters from standoff positions without relying on scarce submarines, surface ships, or other exquisite manned launch platforms. Its 250 lbs of modular payload capacity enables real operational impact beyond short-range sensing. By combining range, endurance, payload delivery, and affordability, Ghostfin gives these operators an attritable undersea capability that can get to the fight, remain on station, project undersea power from distributed or austere launch points, and reduce risk to high-value assets.
q3_capability_contribution: A 1000 nmi range, 4-man carryable UUV with 250 lbs of payload capacity.
q4_supply_constraints: Rapid scale requires a clear demand signal to raise new IRAD funds for production. We reduce supply risk through COTS parts and in-house sensor/electromechanical parts production.
q6_unit_cost: $500K/unit now at 1 unit/month; $250K/unit projected at 5 units/month.
q7_measuring_performance: Range, mission endurance, payload carried, and data collected per mission
q8_competitive_advantage: Hybrid-electric powertrain; no comparable industry alternative exists today.
q9_technical_maturity: (3) I have tested my prototype / solution and it works.
q10_integration: NSWC PC has purchased Ghostfin vehicles for T&E, and Ghostfin was at SONIC SPEAR 26. Ghostfin will also participate in OUSW(R&E) MDCA and JREX experimentation this fall, and is slated for participation at Silent Swarm, Gray Flag, BARB 26, REPMUS, Maritime Big Play, and TOEE mACE 26.3/4. UUVGRU will also run Ghostfin at the UUV Confidence Course in August 2026.

offering_name: Eclipse X9 Distributed Composite Manufacturing for Austere Logistics
description: Voltage Vessels delivers the Eclipse X9 Expeditionary Manufacturing Cell, a forward additive manufacturing capability for rapid production and repair of rugged composite mission hardware in contested and distributed environments. The system is built around Eclipse X9, a reinforced thermoplastic composite feedstock engineered for harsh-environment performance, structural stability, and repairability. It is intended to produce mission-relevant parts such as payload housings, battery compartments, sensor mounts, electronics enclosures, protective shrouds, brackets, covers, and other field-replaceable components for unmanned and expeditionary systems. The capability combines feedstock readiness, additive manufacturing, post-processing and inspection, and digital thread / configuration control into a repeatable workflow that can be deployed closer to the point of need. This reduces dependence on long supply chains, lowers sustainment burden, and enables rapid iteration and localized replacement of critical hardware.
differentiator: Voltage’s differentiator is that it is not just a printer or just a material. It is a mission-focused hardware production capability built around a rugged composite platform, controlled manufacturing workflow, and field repair logic. Eclipse X9 is designed for harsh operational environments and offers a combination of structural performance, low water absorption, corrosion resistance, non-conductive behavior, and repairability that is well suited to distributed sustainment and unmanned system hardware. The capability is designed to scale through standardized feedstock, repeatable process parameters, and part-library driven production rather than one-off prototyping. Unlike traditional supply models that rely on long lead times and brittle replacement chains, Voltage enables localized manufacture and rapid regeneration of small but mission-critical parts at the point of need. That makes it directly relevant to contested logistics, where tempo is often lost not because entire platforms fail, but because simple structural and packaging components are unavailable or slow to replace.
q1_problem_understanding: Voltage enhances Joint Force capability by shifting critical mission hardware from long supply chains to forward digital production. The Eclipse X9 Expeditionary Manufacturing Cell enables rapid manufacture and repair of rugged composite parts including payload housings, battery compartments, sensor mounts, electronics enclosures, protective shrouds, brackets, and other field-replaceable components for unmanned and expeditionary systems. This improves readiness in contested logistics environments where simple structural or packaging parts can delay operations when resupply is slow or unavailable. Eclipse X9 combines structural performance, low water absorption, corrosion resistance, non-conductive behavior, and repairability, making it well suited for distributed sustainment, modular mission hardware, and localized fabrication that preserves tempo and reduces sustainment burden.
q3_capability_contribution: Hardware platform for rugged mission part production and repair
q4_supply_constraints: Scales through U.S. compounding partners and distributed LFAM deployment. Domestic inputs and repeatable digital workflows reduce single-point supply and manufacturing risk.
q6_unit_cost: $8 to $15 per kg pellet. $100.00 a kg Filament Roll prices drop when you scale.
q7_measuring_performance: Measured by strength, durability, print repeatability, and field-use fit.
q8_competitive_advantage: Rapid local production and repair of rugged composite mission hardware.
q9_technical_maturity: (3) I have tested my prototype / solution and it works.
q10_integration: Yes. Most recently, Voltage demonstrated its drone platform, Eclipse X9 material, and printability at Camp Pendleton for ARFL, ONR, and Army stakeholders. Voltage also has an active NIWC Pacific CRADA, has supported EOD-related printed payload trials with Marines in Kaneohe, and is preparing for potential evaluation in the Philippines with Army and Navy stakeholders.
q12_security_preference: I do not have an active security clearance.

description: T2S Solutions has been developing a Counter Surveillance Reconnaissance (CSR) Increment 1 prototype since October 2024. This effort was funded by the competitively awarded Multi-Domain Multi-Tier System of Systems Prototyping OTA contract aligned to the former All Domain Sensing Cross Functional Team. Intent for Increment 1 is to deliver the prototype to the PdM TSS in 4QFY26 for follow-on use by Army space formations to assist with incremental development and accelerate POR fielding schedule outlined in the CSR ACDD development timelines. T2S conducted system component research and assessment and gained ADS CFT approval for baseline component configuration. Both PdL TSS and TID-SS (formerly ACM SHA) concurred with the recommended system configuration. The prototype consists of a C2 orchestrator that integrates a Mission Planning Tool (MPT) and various effectors. Activities to date have validated message traffic routing from the MPT at JWICS, through a guard to the Orchestrator at both SIPR and SBU and to an effector controller. This architecture validates cross domain connectivity at both classified and unclassified levels. T2S is developing Inc. 1 with warfighter input. T2S is integrated with 1MDTF’s Innovation Working Group and incorporating their feedback in the development. T2S has had multiple engagements with 1MDTF and USARPAC and was onboarded to the MDO Live IATT in March 2026. The Inc 1 was also onboarded to the JMC IATT in April 2026 to support demonstration at PCC6 in July 2026. The MDO Live IATT is valid until January 2027 which will support follow-on experimentation and incremental development with the 1MDTF.
differentiator: Government owned solution that can integrate effectors from multiple vendors. As new counter sensing effectors come online, only a low level of effort will be required to integrate the new capabilities. Providing only the coordination and orchestration allows T2S to work with the government to select best of breed effectors. The solution provided does not lock the government into a specific vendor and
